component.name: LeafMD
component.summary: Read and edit markdown your way

description.p: LeafMD is a markdown viewer and editor that keeps things simple. Read a document cleanly formatted, work directly in the raw text, or see both side by side and watch your changes appear as you type.

Rather than trying to do everything, LeafMD focuses on doing the essentials well. It is ready to use the moment you open it, and the few options it has stay out of your way, so you can focus on reading and writing.

ul.li: Switch between formatted, raw and split views with one click or Ctrl+1, 2 and 3
A formatted-only view for pure, distraction-free reading, and a Distraction Free mode that hides everything but your document
Tabs keep several documents in one window, and reopen when you start LeafMD again
An optional, resizable side panel shows the folder of the document you're looking at as a tree, for moving between documents
The side panel's Headings page lists the document's headings, so any section is one click away
A word count and reading time sit quietly in the corner, and count your selection too
Edit the raw text with the formatted view updating as you type
A formatting bar adds bold, links, lists, headings, tables and more for you
Lists continue themselves when you press Enter, pasting a web address over text makes a link, and dropping an image inserts a link to it
Misspelt words are underlined as you type, with suggestions a right-click away
A built-in markdown cheatsheet shows the common syntax at a glance
Find and replace, in the raw text or the formatted document
Print the formatted document, or export it as a PDF or as a single web page that opens in any browser
A banner tells you when another app changes your file, and nothing is overwritten without asking
In split view, both sides scroll together
Supports tables, task lists, footnotes and other GitHub-style markdown
Code blocks that name their language are coloured, with language names suggested as you type them
Open files, or a whole folder with leafmd ., from a terminal with an optional short leafmd command
Choose the fonts for the raw text and the formatted view, or zoom in and out with Ctrl+plus and Ctrl+minus
Looks at home on GNOME, following your light or dark style and your accent colour, or stays light or dark if you prefer

screenshot.caption: Edit markdown with the formatting bar
Watch your changes appear side by side as you type

description.p: Colourful code, and pictures with a drag.

ul.li: Code blocks that name their language, like ```python or ```bash, are now coloured in the formatted view, when printing and in exports, in light and dark
Type ``` and the first letter of a language to pick its name from a list
Drop an image from your file manager onto the raw text to insert a link to it, with the path worked out for you
The question about unsaved changes now fits any window size, even while you resize it, without words left alone on a line
Spaces at the end of a line no longer show a yellow bar in the raw text

description.p: Choose whether LeafMD is light or dark.

ul.li: Preferences has a new Style choice: Follow System, Light or Dark. Light or Dark keeps LeafMD that way whatever your desktop uses, and Follow System matches your desktop as before
The choice changes every LeafMD window straight away, including the raw text and the formatted view, and LeafMD remembers it

description.p: A fix for the Files panel.

ul.li: A new document saved into the folder the side panel is showing no longer appears greyed out until it's saved a second time
Empty markdown and text files show normally in the side panel and can be opened

description.p: The Files panel now always shows where the document you're reading lives.

ul.li: The panel shows the folder of the document you're looking at, and follows it when you switch tabs, open a file or save somewhere new, including files in subfolders
An up arrow at the top of the panel shows the folder above, until you switch tabs
Open Folder… opens the folder in a new window when the current one already has a document open
A new, unsaved document no longer shows the folder of the document you were on before
About now credits libspelling, the library behind spell checking

description.p: LeafMD now checks your spelling as you write.

ul.li: Misspelt words in the raw text get a red wavy underline. Code and web addresses are left alone
Right-click an underlined word for suggested spellings, or choose Add to Dictionary or Ignore
Check Spelling in the main menu turns it off or on in every window, and Languages in the right-click menu switches language. It starts in your system's language
Help, Keyboard Shortcuts and the Markdown Cheatsheet no longer open with their first row outlined when opened from the keyboard

description.p: Print your documents, or save them as a PDF or a web page.

ul.li: Print the formatted document with Ctrl+P or Print… in the main menu, whichever view is showing. Pages are always dark text on white, at the size set in Preferences
Export as PDF… saves the formatted document as a PDF that looks the same as the printout
Export as HTML… saves a single web page that opens in any browser. Pictures from your computer are packed inside, so it still works after being emailed, and it goes light or dark to match the reader
Making a window narrower no longer hides the selected tab in the tab bar

description.p: Make room for long names in the side panel.

ul.li: Drag the line between the side panel and the document to make the panel wider or narrower. LeafMD remembers the width for new windows and next time
When the window gets narrower, the panel shrinks first, so the document keeps its room
Hover over a file or folder in the side panel to see its whole name
Fixed LeafMD closing when a link was clicked on a desktop with nothing set up to open it. It now says it couldn't open the link

description.p: Find your way around a document, and see how long it is.

ul.li: The side panel has a new Headings page listing the document's headings. Click one to jump straight there, and the section you're reading is highlighted as you scroll
Switch between Files and Headings with the buttons along the bottom of the side panel. It opens on the page you used last
The bottom-right corner shows the word count and reading time. Select some text to count just that
With Distraction Free and Full Screen both on, Escape now leaves Full Screen first, and a second Escape leaves Distraction Free

description.p: Make the text the size and style you like.

ul.li: Preferences (Ctrl+, or the main menu) lets you choose the font, style and size for the raw text and for the formatted view. Changes show straight away in every window, and Reset puts a font back
Zoom in and out with Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus, or hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel. Ctrl+0 goes back to normal, and the top of the main menu shows how far you've zoomed
Zoom covers every tab in a window, and starts at 100% each time LeafMD opens

description.p: LeafMD has a fresh look that fits right in with GNOME, and a Distraction Free mode for when you just want your words.

ul.li: The formatted view has a new look: GNOME-style checkboxes, tables as rounded cards, cleaner headings, and links and ticked boxes in the accent colour you choose in GNOME Settings
The raw text has more room to breathe, and in Raw view it sits in a comfortable column down the middle of the window
Line numbers are now off unless you turn them on with Line Numbers in the main menu
Distraction Free (Ctrl+Shift+D) hides everything but your document. Move the pointer to the top of the window to bring the bars back, and press Escape to leave
Full Screen (F11) fills the screen, with or without Distraction Free
Dragging a tab onto an empty window now moves it there, instead of opening another window

description.p: LeafMD now has a side panel that shows the folder you're working in, so the next document is one click away.

ul.li: Press F9, or click the new button at the left of the header bar, to open the side panel. It stays open until you close it
The panel shows a folder as a tree. Click a file to open it in a tab. The document you're looking at is highlighted
The tree follows the document you're looking at. To keep one folder in the panel while you work in it, choose it with Open Folder… (Ctrl+Shift+O) or run leafmd . in a terminal
Images, PDFs and other files LeafMD can't open are greyed out, and hidden files aren't listed
In a narrow window, the panel slides over the document
Split view now always starts with the divider in the middle, even after reopening a maximized window

description.p: LeafMD now has tabs, so one window can hold everything you're working on.

ul.li: Any file you open gets its own tab, including from your file manager and from links. The tab bar appears once a window has two documents
Each tab keeps its own text, view, undo history, find bar and banner
Drag a tab to reorder it, move it to another window or pull it out into a new one
Starting LeafMD brings back the saved files from the window you closed last, in the same tabs
Keyboard changes: Ctrl+T starts a new document, Ctrl+N opens a new window, and Ctrl+W closes the tab rather than the window. Ctrl+Q closes the window with all its tabs
Right-clicking LeafMD's icon offers New Window
Ctrl+Z now works straight after clicking Replace All
If you set up the short leafmd command before this version, run the setup again to use options like --new-window from any folder. See leafmd.app for the steps

description.p: LeafMD is now easier to use from a terminal.

ul.li: Starting LeafMD from a terminal now gives the terminal back straight away, and LeafMD stays open if you close the terminal
A one-time setup adds a short leafmd command, so leafmd notes.md opens a file. Help links to the steps
The new --foreground option keeps LeafMD attached to the terminal, to show its messages when something goes wrong

description.p: LeafMD now fits windows as small as 360 by 300 pixels. In a narrow window, the New, Save and Find buttons and the view buttons move to a bar along the bottom, and the find bar wraps onto extra rows.

ul.li: A banner now tells you when another app changes or deletes your open file, so you can reload it or keep what you have. Save also asks before replacing a version you haven't seen
A new button next to Open starts a new document with one click
Save is now a labelled button, just left of the view switcher
Open and its recent files arrow now look like one raised button
LeafMD now draws its own icons for the window's buttons, Find, the main menu and more, so they look the same on every Linux distribution
New Close Document item in the main menu takes you back to the "No Document Open" page, and LeafMD starts there next time too
Clear Recent Files now also forgets your last file, and is available even when the only recent file is the one you have open
Icons now look the same on every Linux distribution, including a floppy disk for Save
The Keyboard Shortcuts window is simpler, with no search box, and now also lists Ctrl+Q
Saving a file now moves it to the top of your recent files

description.p: LeafMD's page in your app store now shows screenshots of the formatted, raw and split views. Nothing else changes.
The first release of LeafMD, a simple markdown viewer and editor.

ul.li: Read a document formatted, edit the raw text, or see both side by side as you type
A formatting bar and a built-in cheatsheet for bold, links, lists, headings, tables and more
Lists continue when you press Enter, and pasting a web address over text makes a link
Find and replace, in the raw text or the formatted document
Install from leafmd.app, and get updates through your app store
